source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of constructors and destructors (PDF 58).

items: Constructor: ek khaas function jo class ke variables ko shuru ki value deta (initialize karta) hai. Python mein __init__() method object bante hi us ki properties set karta hai.

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"class Car:": Car naam ki class banti hai.
"def __init__(self , color):": constructor; jab bhi Car ka naya object banega, yeh khud chalega aur color lega.
"self . color = color": di hui color object ke andar mehfooz (save) ho jati hai. Dot ke aas paas spaces ka koi asar nahi.
Yeh sirf class ki shakal (definition) hai; koi object nahi banaya gaya, is liye chalane par screen par kuch nahi aata. Misaal ke taur par my_car = Car("red") likhne se object banega aur my_car.color "red" hoga.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab constructor ki misaal ek hi line mein chhapti hai (class Car: def __init__... ); aise SyntaxError aata hai. Sahi shakal oopar hai.

items: Destructor: __del__() method tab chalta hai jab object delete hota hai. Yeh cleanup (safai) ke kaam aata hai.

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"class Car:" aur "def __init__(self, color):": pehle jaisa constructor jo object bante waqt color rakhta hai.
"def __del__(self) :": destructor; jab object delete hota hai (maslan del se, ya program khatam hone par) to yeh khud chalta hai.
"print("Car with color", self.color , "is being deleted . ")": delete hote waqt message dikhata hai, jaise cleanup (safai) ki khabar.
Yeh sirf class ki definition hai; koi object nahi bana, is liye chalane par kuch print nahi hota. Agar c = Car("red") aur phir del c likhein to "Car with color red is being deleted . " aayega (kitab ki spacing ke saath).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab ke print mein "is being deleted . " se pehle quote nahi (self.color ,  is being deleted . ")); aise SyntaxError aata hai. Sahi: print("Car with color", self.color, "is being deleted.").

Yeh destructor object delete hone par message print karta hai, jo batata hai ke cleanup ho raha hai. Maslan c = Car("red") ke baad del c likhne par "Car with color red is being deleted . " print hota hai.
Wazahat: Car class color attribute ke saath banti hai, aur jab us ka koi object delete hota hai to message batata hai ke us color wali car hatayi ja rahi hai.

blocks.explanation: __init__ object banne par chalta hai; __del__ object delete hone par (maslan del car se ya program ke aakhir mein).

blocks.text: Object bante hi constructor __init__ chalta hai aur del se delete hote waqt destructor __del__. color badal kar Run karein aur dekhein dono messages kis tarteeb (order) mein aate hain.

color = "red"
class Car:
    def __init__(self, color):
        self.color = color
        print("Constructor: car with color", self.color, "created.")
    def __del__(self):
        print("Destructor: car with color", self.color, "is being deleted.")
my_car = Car(color)
print("Car is in use. Color:", my_car.color)
del my_car
print("Program finished.")

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"color = "red"": car ka rang.
"def __init__(self, color):": constructor; color rakhta hai aur foran "Constructor: ..." wala message print karta hai.
"def __del__(self):": destructor; object delete hote waqt "Destructor: ..." wala message print karta hai.
"my_car = Car(color)": object banta hai, is liye constructor chalta hai.
"print("Car is in use. Color:", my_car.color)": object istemal ho raha hai.
"del my_car": object delete hota hai, is liye isi waqt destructor chalta hai.
"print("Program finished.")": aakhri line.
Output: chaar lines is tarteeb se: "Constructor: car with color red created.", "Car is in use. Color: red", "Destructor: car with color red is being deleted." aur "Program finished.".
Khud try karein: color = "blue" kar ke Run karein: dono messages mein red ki jagah blue aayega, tarteeb wahi rahegi.

items: __init__: object bante waqt; __del__: object delete hote waqt.
